elements.char: Discerning between cycling/circulation and reabsorption.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Enteric reabsorption occurs when a frac-
elements.label: text

elements.char: tion of drug transferred from the arterial bloodstream to the gastrointestinal tract (GIT) is subsequently reab-
elements.label: text

elements.char: sorbed back into the systemic circulation. When this process includes a discrete step, it causes secondary or mul-
elements.label: text

elements.char: tiple peaks in the plasma-concentration–time profile. The most known process of this kind is usually referred to
elements.label: text

elements.char: as enterohepatic cycling or enterohepatic circulation (EHC), however in this work we are making a distinction
elements.label: text

elements.char: and suggesting the use of drug enterohepatic reabsorption (EHR) as a more precise concept. The cycling fraction
elements.label: text

elements.char: of a compound undergoing EHC is the one that completes the cycle liver-gallbladder-gut-liver, diffusing through
elements.label: text

elements.char: the intestinal epithelium in a significant extent, avoiding gut-wall mediated metabolism and resulting efficiently
elements.label: text

elements.char: extracted by the liver. On the other hand, when EHR takes place, the drug reaches the systemic bloodstream
elements.label: text

elements.char: after diffusing through the intestinal epithelium, avoiding the hepatic metabolism and hepatobiliary secretion,
elements.label: text

elements.char: and completing the cycle bloodstream-liver-gallbladder-gut-bloodstream. Therefore, cycling is not a synonym of
elements.label: text

elements.char: reabsorption. Bile acids are the compounds associated with the largest fraction undergoing EHC and are mostly
elements.label: text

elements.char: Methods
elements.label: text

elements.char: Two semi-mechanistic models accounting for key aspects of EHR and EGR were developed for pharmacokinetic
elements.label: text

elements.char: assessment. Although different approaches can be implemented to address the questions raised here, this model-
elements.label: text

elements.char: based approach allowed us to assess the phenomena under study in two ways, addressing the pharmacokinetic
elements.label: text

elements.char: impact of drug enteric secretion and drug reabsorption.
elements.label: text

elements.char: First, to assess the impact of drug hepatobiliary and gastric secretion in primary pharmacokinetic parameters
elements.label: text

elements.char: under models EHR and EGR respectively, theoretical equations were derived and verified against empirical
elements.label: text

elements.char: estimations obtained through deterministic simulations.
elements.label: text

elements.char: Then, to quantitatively assess the impact of drug reabsorption on primary pharmacokinetic parameters,
elements.label: text

elements.char: three drug types showing significant reabsorption were defined by assigning specific values to the first-order rate
elements.label: text

elements.char: constants. Drugs undergoing reabsorption in a significant magnitude share the following characteristics to some
elements.label: text

elements.char: extent: high enteric secretion (hepatobiliary, gastric, or other possible route), high intestinal permeability, and
elements.label: text

elements.char: negligible intestinal elimination. Nevertheless, differences in distribution and elimination among these drugs
elements.label: text

elements.char: could make the reabsorption process dissimilarly meaningful. These differences were evaluated by conducting
elements.label: text

elements.char: simulations with variability in the first-order rate constants for each drug type in both models, estimating the
elements.label: text

elements.char: primary pharmacokinetic parameters for the simulated concentrations by non-compartmental analysis and eval-
elements.label: text

elements.char: uating the correlation between these parameters and the magnitude of drug hepatobiliary (or gastric) secretion.
